🔮 Election Forecast

Projections combine current support levels, canvassing/contact data, voter sentiment, turnout signals, overseas return likelihood, and historical results. They are probabilistic estimates with confidence levels — not guarantees.

Projected Vote Share by Party
Labour Vote Share — History vs Projection
🎚️ Scenario Modeling

Adjust assumptions to test how the projection changes. Move a slider and the projection above updates live.

🗳️ Projected Result by Party — this constituency
🏛️ Federation Projection — every seat, every party

Each seat is projected independently under the current scenario settings. Margin of error is a 95% interval based on the number of voters actually identified in that seat; seats where the projected margin sits inside the error band are flagged as too close to call.

📊 Historical Performance — Labour vs Opposition Parties

National vote-share trend uses every verified national-level result. Seat counts and constituency breakdowns are based on constituency-level results, verified from 1995 onward. Parties with no results shown for a given period did not contest under that name at that level.

📊 Polling Data
🎛️ Model Parameters

Adjust any assumption and the projection re-runs. The two uncertainty dials matter most: national uncertainty is error that hits every seat together (the kind that makes forecasts wrong), and seat-level uncertainty is independent local variation.

🎯 Seat-by-Seat Projection

Win probability comes from how often each party carried the seat across every simulation. Seats are ordered from safest Labour to safest opposition, so the battleground sits in the middle.

📉 Sensitivity — what would change the result
ℹ️ How this model works

Two inputs, blended per seat. The 2022 result is the starting point (past results are the strongest single predictor of how a seat votes). Your live voter-ID data is blended in, weighted by how much of that seat you have actually identified — a seat with 10% coverage leans mostly on history, a seat with 70% coverage leans on your canvass.

Uncertainty is modelled, not assumed away. Every run simulates the election thousands of times. Crucially, error is split into a national component drawn once per simulation and applied to every seat together, plus an independent local component per seat. Treating seats as independent is the classic modelling error that makes forecasts look far more confident than they should be.

What the outputs mean. A "72% chance of a majority" means Labour won 6+ seats in 72% of simulations — not that it will win 72% of the vote. The tipping-point seat is the one that delivers the majority when seats are ranked by safety; it is where a marginal dollar or hour is worth most.

Limits worth stating. The model has no public opinion polling, so it cannot see late national swings that your canvass has not picked up. It assumes the same parties contest as in 2022. Raise the national uncertainty dial to reflect that.

🎯 Operating Scope — what the whole app shows

Narrow every screen — dashboards, voters, canvassing, GOTV, maps, reports — to a level of the federation. This is a view filter: it can never show you more than your role already permits.

🔓 Data Export Access

Only Candidate, Chief Technical Manager, Deputy Application Manager, and specifically-authorized users can export or download data. If you need it, request access below — an approver is notified and can approve or decline with a reason.

🔑 Custom Roles

Define new roles beyond the built-in set and choose exactly which permissions each one grants. Roles created here appear in the Add User role list. Global administration (user/password management, security logs, system settings) can never be granted through a custom role — those stay reserved to the built-in global roles.

🗳️ Polling Division Boxes

Split a polling division into boxes by surname letter range — e.g. Box 1 – Chapel Road (A–M) and Box 2 – Chapel Road (N–Z). Voters are assigned automatically by the first letter of their last name.

⚠️ Data Management — Danger Zone
Read before continuing. These actions permanently delete records from the live database for every user, cannot be undone from inside the app, and are written to the security audit log.
Clear demo / sample data only

Removes only records generated by the demo seed. Real imported data (such as the Constituency 4 register) is preserved.

Clear one constituency

Deletes all voters, households, casework, rides and related records for a single constituency — synthetic and real alike.

Clear ALL campaign data

Empties every operational table across the entire federation. User accounts, roles and the audit log are kept.

Pins without saved coordinates are placed at an approximate polling-division / constituency position (clearly labelled). Tap a pin to view or correct its location. Location data is sensitive — access is scoped to your assigned constituencies and all activity is audit-logged.

Record Donation

Donations are recorded against a constituency and are visible only to users assigned to it. All entries, edits, and exports are audit-logged. Keep donor records in line with applicable campaign-finance and data-protection rules.

🔗 Online Payment Links

Card, bank/ACH, and PayPal payments are processed by a payment provider — never inside this app (secret keys and card data must stay server-side for PCI compliance). Paste your hosted payment/donation links below. Supporters click through to pay; confirmed payments come back as donation records.

How to go fully automatic (webhooks)
  1. Create the payment links in Stripe/PayPal (enable recurring for subscriptions).
  2. Deploy a Supabase Edge Function to receive the provider's webhook; keep the secret key there.
  3. On payment succeeded, insert a row into the donations table with the constituency passed as link metadata.
  4. The donation then appears here automatically, marked Received with the transaction ID.

🗺️ Google Maps API Key

The Voter Map uses Google Maps for St. Kitts & Nevis streets, satellite, Street View, and address search. Paste your key below.

How to get a key
  1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and create/select a project.
  2. Enable Maps JavaScript API, Places API, and Geocoding API.
  3. Create an API key under Credentials.
  4. Enable billing (Google gives ~$200/month free credit).
  5. Restrict the key to your site's web address.
